about.title: Dana Point Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Dana Point saw 3 traffic deaths among its 81 reported injury collisions in the most recent final year, with crashes clustering on Friday afternoons along Pacific Coast Highway, I-5, Stonehill Drive, and Rt 1. Behind each of those numbers is a family trying to make sense of a sudden, permanent loss. California law gives certain surviving spouses, domestic partners, children, and in some cases other dependents the right to bring a wrongful death claim, but that right comes with a strict two-year window from the date of death, sometimes shorter if a government entity is involved. Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their companionship and guidance. We handle wrongful death claims on contingency, so there's nothing owed unless a recovery is made. You focus on your family. We'll focus on your case.

whyChoose.title: Why Dana Point Families Choose Us

items.title: Standing Rules, Explained Clearly
items.desc: California limits who can file a wrongful death claim, prioritizing spouses, domestic partners, and children before other dependents or heirs. We can walk your family through exactly where you stand.

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives families two years from the date of death to file, though claims against a government entity often require action much sooner. Getting started early protects your options.

items.title: Losses Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: A wrongful death claim isn't only about funeral and burial costs; it can also account for lost financial support and the loss of a loved one's companionship and guidance. We can help make sure nothing is overlooked.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have first standing to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may be able to bring the claim. We can review your family's specific situation to confirm eligibility.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in Dana Point?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If the crash involved a government-owned road or vehicle, such as certain sections near Stonehill Drive or I-5 interchanges, the deadline to act can be much shorter. It's worth speaking with us as soon as you're able.

items.question: What can a wrongful death claim actually recover?
items.answer: Recoverable losses typically include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have contributed, and compensation for the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Every family's losses look different, and we can help identify what applies to yours. This is separate from any criminal case that may also be pending.
